---
title: "Level-Set Topology Optimization (OpenLSTO)"
toc: true
---

## Description

Level-set topology optimization represents the design boundary implicitly as
the zero contour of a signed-distance function and moves it with shape
sensitivities, so the boundary stays crisp throughout the optimization (no
intermediate densities). This tutorial uses the `TopOpt.OpenLSTO` submodule, a
self-contained Julia translation of [OpenLSTO](https://github.com/M2DOLab/OpenLSTO).

We solve two problems:

- **Compliance minimization** on a cantilever (left edge fixed, downward load
  at the midpoint of the right edge) under a volume-fraction constraint.
- **Stress minimization** on an L-beam, minimizing the p-norm of the von
  Mises stress under a volume-fraction constraint.

A 3D level-set compliance solver ([`compliance_minimization_3d`](../reference/OpenLSTO.md))
with marching-cubes boundary discretization is also available.

[← Back to tutorials](index.html)

## Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
using TopOpt
using TopOpt.OpenLSTO
using WGLMakie
WGLMakie.activate!(; resize_to=:parent)
using Bonito
if haskey(ENV, "QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR")
    Bonito.Page(exportable=true, offline=true)
else
    Bonito.browser_display()
end
display_app(app) = display(app)
```

## Compliance minimization

`compliance_minimization` runs the level-set compliance loop. The level-set
grid is seeded with a "Swiss cheese" arrangement of circular holes by
default (which requires a mesh of at least about 75×75); for a smaller mesh
you pass your own `LevelSetHole` list:

```{julia}
#| output: false
holes = [
    LevelSetHole(16, 8, 4), LevelSetHole(32, 8, 4), LevelSetHole(48, 8, 4),
    LevelSetHole(24, 16, 4), LevelSetHole(40, 16, 4), LevelSetHole(56, 16, 4),
    LevelSetHole(16, 24, 4), LevelSetHole(32, 24, 4), LevelSetHole(48, 24, 4),
]
result = compliance_minimization(; nelx=80, nely=40, holes=holes, verbose=false)
```

The returned `LevelSetResult` holds the final level set, its discretized
boundary, the finite element study and sensitivities, and the per-iteration
objective and area-fraction histories:

```{julia}
println("iterations: ", length(result.objectives))
println("final compliance: ", round(result.objectives[end]; digits=4))
println("final area fraction: ", round(result.areas[end]; digits=4))
```

## Visualize the design

`visualize(::LevelSetResult)` converts the level-set design to a
`PointLoadCantilever` problem on the same grid and shows the per-cell area
fractions as the density field, so the same load/support arrows and static
viewer apply as for SIMP results:

```{julia}
#| label: fig-levelset
#| fig-cap: "Level-set compliance minimization: cantilever design"
app = visualize(result; static=true)
display_app(app)
```

## Stress minimization (L-beam)

`stress_minimization` minimizes the p-norm of the von Mises stress on an
L-beam (top edge fixed, downward load on the right edge at 2/5 height):

```{julia}
#| output: false
lresult = stress_minimization(;
    nelx=40, nely=40, max_iterations=40,
    holes=[LevelSetHole(8, 8, 5), LevelSetHole(8, 20, 5), LevelSetHole(20, 8, 5)],
    verbose=false,
)
```

```{julia}
println("iterations: ", length(lresult.objectives))
println("final p-norm stress: ", round(lresult.objectives[end]; digits=4))
println("max von Mises stress: ", round(lresult.sensitivities.von_mises_max; digits=4))
```

The area fractions of the stress result can be shown with the same viewer
(load/support arrows describe the equivalent cantilever, so for the L-beam
they are indicative only):

```{julia}
#| label: fig-levelset-stress
#| fig-cap: "Level-set stress minimization: L-beam design"
app = visualize(lresult; static=true)
display_app(app)
```

## Hole nucleation

When the volume constraint is far from being met, `compliance_minimization`
can nucleate new holes (a port of OpenLSTO's `projects/hole_creation`) rather
than only moving the existing boundary. Enable it with `hole_nucleation=true`:

```{julia}
#| output: false
hresult = compliance_minimization(;
    nelx=40, nely=20,
    holes=[LevelSetHole(8, 4, 2), LevelSetHole(16, 4, 2), LevelSetHole(24, 4, 2),
           LevelSetHole(12, 8, 2), LevelSetHole(20, 8, 2), LevelSetHole(28, 8, 2),
           LevelSetHole(8, 12, 2), LevelSetHole(16, 12, 2), LevelSetHole(24, 12, 2)],
    hole_nucleation=true, max_iterations=8, verbose=false,
)
```

```{julia}
println("final compliance: ", round(hresult.objectives[end]; digits=4))
```

## 3D level-set

A 3D level-set solver discretizes the boundary with marching cubes and drives
a trilinear-hex finite element solve; the final surface can be exported as an
STL:

```{julia}
#| output: false
r3 = compliance_minimization_3d(; nelx=10, nely=5, nelz=5, max_iterations=4, verbose=false)
write_stl(r3.level_set, "mystlfile.stl")
```

```{julia}
println("final compliance: ", round(r3.compliances[end]; digits=4))
println("wrote ", r3.level_set.num_triangles, " triangles to mystlfile.stl")
```

The 3D design can be visualized with the same viewer as a 3D SIMP result:

```{julia}
#| label: fig-levelset-3d
#| fig-cap: "Level-set compliance minimization: 3D cantilever design"
app = visualize(r3.level_set; static=true)
display_app(app)
```

## Exporting the design

The OpenLSTO module mirrors OpenLSTO's own VTK/TXT writers for the level-set
function and area fractions:

```{julia}
#| output: false
out = mktempdir()
save_level_set_vtk(result.level_set, 1; output_directory=out)
save_area_fractions_vtk(result.level_set.mesh, 1; output_directory=out)
save_boundary_segments_txt(result.boundary, 1; output_directory=out)
```

```{julia}
println(readdir(out))
```
